suggestions.reason: Four of the five assertions (1, 2, 3, 4) are satisfied by *absence*. A one-line reply — 'No, this reads human.' — would pass all four, and would arguably pass assertion 5 with a five-word gesture at length. The suite therefore cannot distinguish this genuinely substantive report from a terse non-answer. Add at least one positive-substance assertion, e.g. 'the response names the specific low-signal item it did find (showcases / AI-VOCAB) and marks it as below threshold rather than omitting it entirely' — that discriminates between correct restraint and lazy restraint, which is the actual failure mode this eval cares about.

suggestions.assertion: The response gives a reason for restraint, such as a hit count or rate relative to the text's length, the small number of distinct patterns, or the absence of structural tells
suggestions.reason: The disjunction is so wide ('or ... or ...') that almost any hand-wave qualifies — 'there just aren't many tells here' satisfies 'a small number of distinct patterns' on a charitable read. Tighten to require a quantity actually tied to the skill's threshold table: a density figure per 100 words AND a pattern-spread count, or an explicit citation of the row of the threshold table being applied.

No assertion checks the *accuracy* of the numbers the response cites, and this run contains a wrong one that went completely uncaught: the sentence-length list '4, 8, 9, 10, 12, 20, 24, 25, 27' sums to 139 while the same document reports 138 words (the correct series has two 24s). Since the whole verdict rests on hand-measured rates, an assertion like 'any word counts, comma rates, or sentence-length figures cited are correct for the source text' would catch fabricated or sloppy measurement — the most dangerous silent failure for this skill.

No assertion covers over-flagging generally. Assertions 1 and 2 pre-name the two false positives the eval author anticipated (Moreover, VAGUE-CONNECT), but a response could invent a different bogus finding — INFLATION on 'held at 81 percent', GAP-SPECULATION on 'We have not yet analysed' — and still pass every assertion including 3, as long as it landed on 'human'. Add a catch-all: 'the response asserts no finding other than, at most, the single AI-VOCAB hit on showcases.'

suggestions.assertion: The response does not perform a rewrite of the text, in full or of any paragraph, even as an optional extra; it reports findings only, with at most a one-clause fix suggestion per finding
suggestions.reason: 'One-clause fix suggestion' is left to grader judgment. The response here supplied a replacement phrase spanning most of a clause, which I judged compliant against SKILL.md:68's identical wording — but a grader without that line in hand could go either way. Cite the SKILL.md sentence in the assertion, or bound it mechanically (e.g. 'no proposed replacement exceeds one sentence, and none is offered for text that was not flagged').

eval_feedback.overall: The suite correctly gates the behaviour this eval was built for — the isolated 'Moreover' false positive — and the run passes all five cleanly on strong, quotable evidence. The weakness is that the suite is almost entirely composed of negative assertions, so it measures what the response avoided saying and barely measures whether it did any real work. Two additions would fix that: one assertion on positive substance (the correctly-scoped low-signal finding) and one on numerical accuracy (which would have caught the sentence-length miscount in this very run).
